### Sources

The daily source program screened five new source families: Asianfanfics, Quotev, FictionPress, MediaMiner, and Honeyfeed. Asianfanfics, FictionPress, and Honeyfeed received complete bounded source-specific audits for the capabilities actually considered, satisfying the minimum complete-audit target. Asianfanfics passed as the cycle's new integration and shipped through pull request #120 as an eighth route in `Fanfiction Discovery Starter`.

Asianfanfics' public Stories browse is accessible through ordinary reader navigation and exposes discovery views alongside origin-owned Members Only, Subscribers Only, crowdfunding, and age/access boundaries. Its current first-party terms protect site/user content and constrain copying or storing substantial portions. WebNR therefore admits only the normal first-party browse destination plus WebNR-authored labels and description; it performs no catalog polling, metadata extraction, account automation, gated-content access, downloads, or story-text copying.

Quotev's public Fanfiction Browse rendered, but the operating environment did not provide a reliable text view of the current first-party terms body or an explicit supported machine interface, so it remains deferred rather than being admitted from third-party policy copies. MediaMiner remained readable, including current fanfiction category pages, but sufficiently current first-party machine-access/terms evidence was not obtained in the bounded audit; it also remains deferred. FictionPress and Honeyfeed had usable first-party terms evidence but belong more naturally to original-fiction / English-serial discovery lanes, and their terms do not justify a metadata mirror; neither was forced into the fanfiction starter simply to increase route count.

The rotating health review rechecked FanFiction.Net search, Fimfiction search/developer documentation, and Scribble Hub Series Finder/Fanfiction discovery. Their admitted public discovery surfaces remained available.

The Fimfiction richer-interface audit was advanced to a concrete dependency rather than left as a generic `link-only` excuse. Current first-party developer documentation states that API interactions use OAuth2, and current Application Management documentation says new API applications must presently be created by Fimfiction after the developer contacts the site operator. The documented `GET /stories` contract is specific enough to design a bounded adapter around search/filter/sort and cursor pagination, but WebNR has no registered Fimfiction application/client identity in the repository. No credential was invented, embedded, requested through a user account, or worked around. A future adapter should begin only after that application identity exists, then implement and test OAuth transport, rate-limit/backoff, cache, stable identity, sparse fields, cursor pagination, response/timeout bounds, provenance, attribution, and update/deletion semantics with versioned fixtures.

AO3 remains admitted for normal discovery, and canonical-tag Atom remains a richer machine-interface candidate. Its remaining work is WebNR runtime transport and identity/update/response-bound fixtures rather than an assumed general API.
